r0.why: Seventh planet, cyan ice giant, volatiles, rocky core, H/He atmosphere, 3rd diameter/4th mass all in [1,2,3,7,8].

r1.why: 82.23 tilt, retrograde 17h14m, 84-year orbit and 42/42 years of light/dark from [5,6].

r2.why: Layered clouds, 49 K minimum, trace gases with CO2 from comets, 900 km/h winds, polar cap, erratic clouds, low internal heat all in [4,9,10,11].

r3.why: Rings, magnetosphere, moons; 2% reflectance; 29 moons split 14+5+10; asymmetric magnetosphere possibly darkening rings, per [12-17].

r4.why: Naked-eye but dim and slow, misidentified as star, Flamsteed 1690 as 34 Tauri, Hipparchus 128 BC nonexistent star, per cited sentences.

r5.why: Herschel 13 March 1781 in Bath garden, 6.2-inch reflector, reported as comet; Maskelyne reply; Lexell orbit; Bode; accepted as planet, per cited sentences.

r6.why: First planet classified with a telescope, expanded known boundaries, twice Saturn's distance doubled size, named ~seven decades later, per [19,23,24].

r7.why: Voyager 2 sole visit 1986, telescopes resolve it, Decadal Survey priority 2023-2032, CNSA Tianwen-4 subprobe, per [20,21].
